domain_label: Base44 Delivery & Handoff: Workspace<->GitHub Sync Discipline & 'Unsynced = Unfinished' (single-user study app on Base44)
purpose: Why a build pass is not done until it is on GitHub, grounded in the two observed clobber incidents that made these rules binding — the workspace<->GitHub two-way sync can silently clobber built work (the bkt_evidence fix once; Slice 6.5 Pass 1 on 2026-07-10 lost 4 commits' worth of components + ledger). It fixes the four binding rules (unsynced = unfinished; verify-then-restore after every sync event; docs pushed only between passes; runtime self-checks mandatory) and the Revert re-check, all carried with their PROTOCOL.md [FACT-source] tags.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base scores are heuristic priors and every sync-discipline call is an ESTIMATE synthesized over PROTOCOL.md
the workspace<->GitHub two-way sync can silently clobber built work, observed twice (bkt_evidence; Slice 6.5 Pass 1 on 2026-07-10) [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10]
every fact here is reused verbatim from PROTOCOL.md's Sync-discipline [FACT-source] tag and standing rules; no incident detail or platform behavior is invented, and any gap is [UNKNOWN]
the credit economics of a pass are kb1's and the discuss->edit handoff sequence is kb2's; this KB governs only what makes a pass durable on GitHub
exclusions: the message/integration-credit economics of a pass (kb1)
the discuss->edit handoff sequence and the free-surface routing (kb2) beyond the Revert re-check cross-link
the internal mechanics of git/GitHub sync on the Base44 platform (owned by extint / the platform) beyond the observed clobber behavior and the response rules
the substance of a given acceptance check or runtime self-check (authored by the owning specialist); this KB requires only that they exist, run, and re-run after a Revert
any Base44 platform behavior not documented in PROTOCOL.md's Sync discipline

glossary.definition: The bidirectional sync between the Base44 workspace and GitHub that can silently clobber built work; observed to do so twice, which is why the sync-discipline rules are binding [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The rule that a build pass is not done until it is synced to GitHub; Base44 commits/pushes at the end of every pass BEFORE reporting done, so unsynced work is unfinished work [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

A sync event pulling N commits into the workspace; after ANY such event the last ledgered pass must be diffed against the actual code before advancing, because the sync may have removed built work [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The response to a sync event: diff the last ledgered pass against the actual code; if the code is gone, RESTORE it first and say so explicitly, never advancing the queue over a hole (this exact check caught the Slice 6.5 Pass 1 revert) [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The interval during which a sync can overwrite in-flight built work; a mid-build sync is the clobber window, which is why owner/Codex push documentation to planit only BETWEEN passes, never while a build is in flight [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

A mandatory pair on model/logic code — a version marker plus a behavioral check that refuses a reverted model — kept because rules 1-3 reduce but do not close the clobber window [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].
The self-check component that stamps model/logic code with a version so a silent revert to an older version is detectable at runtime [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The self-check component that refuses to run a reverted model — a behavioral test that fails loudly if the code has rolled back below the expected version [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The first observed clobber: the bkt_evidence fix was silently lost once via a Revert that removed model/logic code without a re-check — the incident that makes the Revert re-check mandatory [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

The second observed clobber: on 2026-07-10 a doc-sync pulled 4 commits and removed the pass's components + ledger entry, caught by the diff-the-last-ledgered-pass check [FACT-source: PROTOCOL.md Sync discipline, added 2026-07-10].

A pass that built and passed acceptance can still be erased by a later sync, so 'built and accepted' is not 'safe' — only 'committed, pushed, and verified-after-sync' is safe. conflict_axes.name: built_is_safe_vs_only_synced_is_safe
conflict_axes.description: Intuition says a built-and-accepted pass is safe, but the two-way sync can silently clobber it, so only synced-and-verified is safe.
poles: treat only synced+verified work as safe
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: a pass is not done until synced to GitHub and verified clean after the next sync

conflict_axes.name: trust_the_sync_vs_treat_it_as_a_clobber
conflict_axes.description: A 'Synced N commits' event can be read as a benign update or as a potential clobber to verify.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: after ANY sync event, diff the last ledgered pass against the code before advancing

conflict_axes.name: report_done_vs_push_first
conflict_axes.description: Momentum pulls toward reporting a pass done before the closing push completes.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: commit/push at the end of the pass BEFORE reporting done; unsynced work is unfinished

conflict_axes.name: free_revert_vs_mandatory_recheck
conflict_axes.description: A Revert is a cheap undo but can silently drop model/logic code, so it carries a mandatory re-check.
poles: treat Revert as a clean undo
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: after any Revert re-run the behavioral self-checks and, for model/logic, the slice's acceptance checks (the bkt loss)

conflict_axes.name: advance_the_queue_vs_restore_the_hole
conflict_axes.description: After a sync reveals missing work, the queue pull pulls toward advancing versus restoring the hole first.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restore clobbered work first and say so explicitly; never advance over a hole

conflict_axes.name: push_docs_anytime_vs_only_between_passes
conflict_axes.description: Owner/Codex could push docs whenever, but a mid-build push opens the clobber window.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: push documentation to planit only between passes, never while a build is in flight

conflict_axes.name: trust_process_rules_vs_runtime_self_checks
conflict_axes.description: Process rules 1-3 could be trusted to fully prevent the clobber, but they only narrow the window, so runtime self-checks stay mandatory.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the version marker + behavioral refusal on model/logic code because rules 1-3 do not close the window

conflict_axes.name: silent_restore_vs_explicit_statement
conflict_axes.description: A clobber could be restored silently or reported explicitly to keep the audit trail.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: say so explicitly when restoring; a silent restore hides a real loss and breaks the audit trail
